correctness.rationale: The count of nonempty disjoint shadows rules out zero markers for n≥2 and forces all shadows to be singletons with one marker. For two adjacent deleted positions, the surviving entries outside those positions keep their positions in both outputs; their ranks differ exactly when their values are strictly between the two deleted values. If no such value exists, the remaining member of the adjacent pair also has the same rank in both outputs. Thus a singleton shadow forces every adjacent pair to differ by 1; a permutation cannot reverse such a walk without repeating a value, so only the two monotone words qualify. This rules out one marker for n≥3. I independently enumerated the displayed codebooks (RESULT.md lines 29–46), not by executing the uploaded checker: for each deletion I replaced each surviving entry by one plus the number of smaller survivors, deduplicated within its parent, and checked cross-parent disjointness, alphabet, and exact coverage by restricting each parent to labels ≤n. For n=1,2,3,4 there were respectively 1,2,6,24 distinct messages and 1,2,16,97 disjoint outputs, agreeing with VERIFY.txt. For n=4 the shadow-size histogram is {1:1,2:1,3:5,4:9,5:5,6:3}. VERIFY.py lines 6–45 is the frozen replay path for the finite certificates; no finite test is needed for the infinite lower bound. No upper bound for n≥5 is certified.
